judgments.rationale: The footer site-map link 'Saiba mais...' (href /saiba-mais) is the title link of a footer column; its list item also holds the nested list Portal do Estado do RS, Agência de Notícias, Agenda do Governador, Secretarias e Órgãos do Estado. That list item is programmatically determined context under the rubric (same list item), and it tells users what the link heads: the group of state-government links. The destination, opened live, is the page 'Saiba mais... - RS.GOV.BR' whose only content is a list of exactly those four child pages (_service/conteudo/pagedlistfilho?id=942 returns them), so the link text with its list item determines its purpose. The claim that nothing around it tells where it goes is false of the capture. The nearest preceding heading ('Descomplica RS') is unrelated but not needed. The live footer has the same markup, so the capture does not differ.

The hero background image (upload 202506) and CSS are the same live, so the capture does not differ. The page offers a working high-contrast switch: the 'Contraste' link in the top bar (white on dark teal, about 6:1) runs stylesheet.selector.js, which enables the alternate style sheet contraste.css and keeps it in a cookie; that sheet lays rgba(0,0,0,0.825) over the hero (.wrapperDigitalRSBusca__filtro) and makes links and buttons white, so in that presentation this white content would sit on a near-black background. G174 (a control that switches to a presentation with sufficient contrast) is listed as sufficient for 1.4.3 and for 1.4.11 when used for identifying user interface components, but it also requires the switched page to conform to every success criterion at the level. I could not render the high-contrast presentation to confirm the element there, nor establish the alternate version's full conformance, and auditors split on whether such a toggle cures a default-presentation contrast failure.
